text:
The monitor is built and committed on `worktree/proposal-flow` (commits `df74c22a` and `8ef74ea2`). All four proofs from the brief passed, and the card says "ready to merge".

**What changed in `Server/health.mjs`:**
- **Only template changes trigger a check.** Saving a `.js`, `.css` or `.html` file under `public/` loads the pages it could break. Saving a `.jsonl`, `.json` or `.md` file is treated as data: no check runs, and the watcher's console says "data only, no check".
- **Each check now also:**
  - flags a stall: any long task over 2 s, or a page still busy 10 s after it starts loading;
  - takes a 1920-wide screenshot into `public/framework/ai/health/shots/<date>/`;
  - counts `JSONL: unknown verb` warnings as one finding.
- **It reports in two places:**
  - to the editing agent, as before;
  - as one line in that agent's task log, written through the validated `append.mjs`. When no task matches, the line goes to the health log instead.
- **One supervisor per tree.** `health-supervisor.mjs` takes a lock, so a second copy started in the same tree exits quietly. Each checkout (main and each worktree) now has its own lock.

**The proofs** (run in the worktree against its own server; files saved in `ai/2026-09-30/proposal-flow/monitor/proof/`):
1. A test page with a 3 s busy loop was flagged as a 3.0 s stall, with a screenshot.
2. A `throw` in `/framework/ai/health/page.js` produced the error finding, and the error check blocked my next edit. Restoring the file brought "0 console errors" and an "ok" line.
3. Appending a line to a `task.jsonl` ran no check.
4. Starting the supervisor twice left exactly one running.

**Things to know:**
- The main tree's supervisor only gets the new single-instance lock after it is restarted once. Saving `health.mjs` does restart the watcher by itself.
- Right now one hand-started `health.mjs` (pid 25824) runs in the main tree, plus a supervisor and watcher in each of three quick-fix worktrees (qf-4, qf-6, qf-9). I didn't touch any of them.
- The proof posted two "not loading" notices into the worktree's `board.jsonl`. I removed exactly those two lines, so the file matches the last commit again.
- Two follow-ups sit outside my fence: `Servex/Pool.js` still gives each worktree slot its own temp folder to get around the old machine-wide lock (harmless now, just unneeded), and `Server/readme.md` doesn't link the new `Server/doc/health.md` yet.
- Per the brief, a layout scan is left for later.

The doc, `Server/doc/health.md`, covers how to run the monitor, what triggers a check, what it looks at and where it reports. The health page's readme, `/framework/ai/health/`, now points to it.

The review finding is fixed in commit `b0a71a66` on `worktree/proposal-flow`. The card says "ready to merge".

- **The finding:** `task_for()` used to look only in today's and yesterday's folders, so a task opened days ago never got its health line. It still checks those two days first. If nothing matches there, it now looks through every task under `ai/` that hasn't landed yet. Each task log is only re-read when it changes, so the wider search is quick (133 ms the first time, 55 ms after).
  - I tested it with a file edited by a task opened five days earlier. The lookup found that task, not a newer task that had already landed and also listed the file. After the old task landed too, the lookup found nothing. The output is in `monitor/proof/task-lookup.log`.
- **Proof 4:** I re-ran it and saved the console output to `monitor/proof/supervisor-twice.log`. The second supervisor printed "already running … exiting quietly" and exited with code 0. The first kept exactly one `health.mjs` running and showed no window. I stopped it afterwards.
- **Notes:**
  - Note 3 was a one-line fix, so I made it. The "data only, no check" console line now prints every 1.5 s even while data files keep changing.
  - I left note 4 alone. It is about two timeouts that aren't coordinated, and the reviewer judged a wrong result unlikely in practice.
- **`review.md`:** each finding has a line under it saying what changed and which commit.
- **Doc:** `Server/doc/health.md` describes the wider task search and links both new proofs.
- **Cleanup:** the test created two scratch task folders, and the worktree's server wrote two lines about them into a `files.jsonl` (plus one new folder). I removed all of it.

Log writes are now checked before anything is written, and a shell append to a `.jsonl` file is blocked. Everything is committed on `worktree/proposal-flow`, and I've said "ready to merge" on the card.

- **One schema:** `.claude/hooks/jsonl-schema.mjs` says what a line may look like in task, day, board, asks and page logs.
- **`append.mjs` checks first:** if a line has no verb, an unknown verb or a missing field, the whole batch is refused and nothing is written. The error prints the right shape.
- **`append_log` checks too:** an entry needs a string `type`. A task-log line sent there by mistake is refused with a pointer to `append.mjs`. This only takes effect after Servex restarts.
- **The guard is on:** `jsonl-guard.mjs` now runs before every Bash and PowerShell command, next to `git-guard.mjs`.
- **Skills and readme:** no skill showed a shell append, so I changed only `new-task`'s verb paragraph. It used to say an unknown verb fails silently, and now points at the schema. The hooks readme now opens with this route.

**Proof:**
- A flat `{"at","task","msg"}` line on a `task.jsonl` is refused: nothing is written and the right shape is printed. `experiment` and `review` lines are accepted.
- The test that compares the schema with the code that reads the logs passes 30 of 30.
- The guard test passes 16 of 16. It blocks 7 kinds of shell append and lets 7 look-alikes through. If the guard itself fails, the command runs.
- Once wired, the guard blocked my own `echo '{}' >>` into a scratch file.
- My [task log](/framework/ai/2026-09-30/proposal-flow/validated-writes/) was written only through `append.mjs`.

**Things you should know:**
- **Many hand-written lines will now be refused.** On the last three days of real logs, 9% of lines would be refused. All of them were written by hand by agents: a `log` with no `at`, a plain-text `log`, or a flat line. The scripts that already use `append.mjs` (`health.mjs`, `task-cost.mjs`) still pass.
- **Card logs are checked loosely.** `page.jsonl` stays open on purpose, because the code that reads cards treats an unknown key as data. Only the overall shape is checked there, plus `message` and `prompt`.
- **Some commit messages get blocked.** The guard reads the command text, so a commit message that quotes `>> x.jsonl` is blocked too. The readme says to reword it.
- **Three verbs aren't shown on the page yet.** `experiment`, `review` and `shots` are in the schema, but the code that shows logs doesn't know them until the verbs-reader minion's change lands. The test allows for that.

**Left, outside my fence:** about 25 node scripts still append to `.jsonl` without the check. They should call the schema's `check()` before writing. The first three to do are `Server/plugins/SocketServer/Append.js` (every browser page appends through it), `Server/review.mjs` and `.claude/hooks/ledger.mjs`. The full list is in the task log.
The drop script is ready. I'm waiting for verbs-reader to commit `JSONL.js` on the branch; a background watch will tell me when it lands.

I made all three changes from the second review. They are committed as `d0c2c4f1` on `worktree/proposal-flow`, and the card says "done".

- **Note 6, stalls:** the monitor now reads the page's long tasks before it resizes the browser to 1920 for the screenshot. The monitor's own relayout can no longer be counted as the page's stall.
- **Note 7, one line per batch:** an edit to a shared module checks up to 8 pages, and it now puts one line on the editing agent's card instead of 8. That line looks like "health: 8 pages — 2 errors, 1 stall, worst /framework/ux/, shots /framework/ai/health/shots/<date>/". A batch of one page still shows that page's full detail. I checked this with the real report code against made-up results; the screenshot path and the agent's task were stand-ins. The output is in `monitor/proof/batch-line.log`.
- **Note 9, the doc:** `Server/doc/health.md` now says that a `.md` change doesn't trigger a check, because you asked for templates, not data. It also says when a broken readme would still be seen: at the page's next template check, or when someone opens its Docs tab.

Each note has a line under it in `review.md` saying what changed and the commit. The card also says that item 8's cheap layout anomaly check is deferred, together with the layout scan.

I started `health.mjs` on the worktree for 6 seconds to make sure it still starts, then stopped it, so nothing of mine is left running.

Review finding 2 is fixed in two commits on `worktree/proposal-flow`, and the schema test passes 33 of 33.

1. **The test change (39f8e7ec):** the schema test now fails if a verb is still listed as `pending` after the reader already has it. Before, it only printed a note. Right after this change, it failed against the verbs-reader minion's uncommitted `JSONL.js`, which already had both verbs.
2. **The pending drop (27e699b6):** once verbs-reader committed `JSONL.js` (39700c9b), I took `experiment` and `review` off the `pending` list. `shots` stays on it because the reader doesn't have it yet.

I added a line with both commits under finding 2 in `review.md`. That file is in the main tree and not on the branch, so I edited it there and left it uncommitted. I also logged the fix in the task log and posted it on the card.

Done. Summary of the work:

**What was built** — `ext/JSONL/JSONL.js` now knows two new verbs and three old line shapes that used to spam the console:

- **`experiment`** and **`review`** render as one line each onto `logs` (no new array): `"try → measure → result"` and `"review: found N, real M, fixed K"`.
- **Flat lines with no verb at all** (a bare `{"at","task","msg"}` day-log line, or an old `{"type":"launch"}` task line) now render as a plain log line instead of warning once per stray key.
- Two more real shapes found live in today's actual logs also got fixed: a bare pre-`assign`-wrapper progress line (`{"now","step","steps",...}`), and a real verb carrying sibling keys that belonged inside its own value (`{"log":"...", "at":"..."}`).

**Proof** — headless on the worktree server: unknown-verb warnings on `/framework/ai2/` went from **76 → 6**; `/framework/ai/` stayed at **0 → 0**. The 6 remaining are a different, unregistered verb pair (`shots`, `bands`) another in-flight task is still inventing today — correctly left alone, outside this task's experiment/review scope. No console errors were introduced; a screenshot of the new demo page showing both lines rendered is linked in the task log.

Committed as `39700c9b` on `worktree/proposal-flow`, docs updated (readme, decisions, task-jsonl, two method pages), and reported **ready to merge** on the card.
MSYS rewrote the URL arguments into paths, so that run loaded nothing. Re-running it with path conversion off.

Stopped, tree clean. I restored the uncommitted anomaly check in `Server/health.mjs` to the branch head, and no proof files had been added for it.

The branch head is now `27e699b6`, another minion's commit. My four commits sit under it, ending with `d0c2c4f1`.

All four review findings are addressed and reported:

1. **readme.md's append example** now points at the validated `node .claude/hooks/append.mjs` route instead of `printf`/`>>`.
2. **`shots` and `bands` registered** — the two verbs `Server/review.mjs` itself writes — removing the last 6 unknown-verb warnings (verified: 6→0 on `/framework/ai2/`, 0→0 on `/framework/ai/`). `bands` is a plain method like `experiment`/`review`; `shots` needed a different route because `TaskJSONL` already has an instance *array* field named `shots` (the plain `shot` verb's own list, read by `ext/AITask`'s `shot_wall()`) — a method of the same name would be shadowed and crash. Solved it with a small `static lines` map plus a `dispatch()` helper in `apply()` that renders a listed verb straight onto `logs` instead of calling it as a method; every other verb dispatches exactly as before. Logged this as a decision with the rejected alternative (renaming the field — has real outside callers, so it's the "ask first" case).
3. **Flat-line docs fixed** (`doc/method/flat.md`, the readme Watch-out bullet, `doc/decisions.md`, `doc/method/apply.md`) — they all claimed a flat line with no readable text still warns, when `apply()` actually folds an `at`-only line into `assign` instead. Docs now match the code.
4. **Card/decisions.md trimmed** — overview description shortened to "Four verbs, one line each — no new array." (confirmed untruncated at 1920 via screenshot), and the three flagged decisions.md paragraphs cut to about half.

Committed as `9cf84e2e` on `worktree/proposal-flow`, same 7-file fence. One item I flagged rather than fixed myself, since it's outside my fence: `.claude/hooks/jsonl-schema.mjs` (owned by the validated-writes minion) now needs `bands` added to its verb list and `shots` dropped from its `pending` array, or `jsonl-schema.test.mjs` fails those two checks. Logged in task.jsonl and on the card. Reported **ready to merge** again.
